item.title: Jeremiyah Love makes immediate statement with touchdown on first career drive for Cardinals
item.description: Jeremiyah Love's NFL debut featured a statement touchdown as the Arizona Cardinals opened their season against the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium.
item.content:encoded:
Jeremiyah Love’s NFL career started off on quite the high note during the Arizona Cardinals’ Week 1 match-up against the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday.

Love immediately became one of the highest-paid running backs in the NFL when the Cardinals took him third overall back in April out of Notre Dame.

As a result, the expectations were quite high for Love given his draft stock, which tagged him as one of the faces of not just the franchise’s future, but the league as a whole.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Love and the Cardinals took the field at SoFi Stadium as underdogs against the Chargers, but an opening drive by quarterback Jacoby Brissett and Arizona’s offense led to a red-zone opportunity that their new running back didn’t squander.

On second-and-goal from the Chargers’ five-yard line, Love got the handoff from Brissett, bounced out to his left, and found a lane to the left pylon and didn’t lose sight of it. Love outraced the Chargers' defender closing in on him, and he scored his first career touchdown in a statement drive from the Cardinals to begin the season.

JEREMIYAH LOVE SIGNS ROOKIE DEAL THAT GIVES HIM MOST GUARANTEED MONEY BY RUNNING BACK BEFORE TAKING NFL SNAP

First-year head coach Mike LaFleur was visibly enthusiastic after the 70-yard opening drive, joining his players in celebration, Love among them. It’s hard not to love (no pun intended) what this dynamic running back can bring his offense in 2026 and beyond.

The Cardinals caught some flak for the pick of Love when they put in their ticket in April. Arizona is a rebuilding team, one that fired ex-head coach Jonathan Gannon and hired LaFleur with the goal of getting the team back on the right track.

With a pick of Love at third overall, it signaled to some that the Cardinals believed they were one offensive weapon away from competing for a playoff berth. On the other hand, the Cardinals need more playmakers on both sides of the ball, and Love did just that during his stellar collegiate career for the Fighting Irish.

Love dealt with an ankle injury throughout training camp, too, which begged the question of how much he’d play for LaFleur in Week 1. As of halftime, with the Cardinals holding a 13-7 lead, Love split carries with veteran Tyler Allgeier, whom Arizona brought in this offseason as a free agent acquisition.

That should be expected for the Cardinals to at least begin the season, with Love and Allgeier sharing the backfield. However, it’s clear that Love’s explosive abilities are there for the Cardinals, and he made his presence known right away in Week 1.

item.title: Josh Allen torches one of NFL's best defenses to make case it's time to move on from 2025 playoff loss
item.description: Josh Allen passed for 334 yards, threw 2 TDs and ran for 2 others as the Buffalo Bills scored 36 points against an elite Houston Texans defense.
item.content:encoded:
Josh Allen finished last season in tears and the sight of one of the NFL's great players sobbing in the Buffalo Bills locker room after a playoff loss to the Denver Broncos led ownership to fire head coach Sean McDermott. That memory of that scene and the burden it put on Allen was buried on Sunday.

Josh Allen played sensationally against the Houston Texans in a stirring 36-31 game this day. And this means stuff:

It means new Bills coach Joe Brady won his head coaching debut.

It means the Bills have just sent the NFL the message that they remain a Super Bowl contender for 2026 because, well, the Texans team they just beat are a Super Bowl contender.

And it means Josh Allen has already joined the MVP race in earnest after he exorcised the ghosts of his horrible postseason performance and that loss which haunted all offseason.

Allen also made the statement that he can indeed play up to his standard even against the Texans.

"We do like Reliant Stadium, woo-hoo!" Allen exclaimed after the game. "It feels good. It feels good to start the season off right. Obviously coach Joe getting his first win as an NFL head coach ... really happy for him. [He] called a heck of a game."

JOSH ALLEN DELIVERS FULL-THROATED UNSOLICITED DEFENSE OF BUFFALO BILLS' HIDEOUS NEW UNIFORMS

The Texans had dominated Allen in five previous games. The Texans won four of those and limited Allen to 196 passing yards per game.

Not this game.

Allen played up to his billing this time. He played like he's one of the league's best players.

He passed for 334 yards and two touchdowns. And he rushed for two touchdowns. Allen was in some way responsible for all four of his team's touchdowns, by either running or passing for them.

Amid all those numbers, Allen tried to put the focus on others.

"It's the players that we got, man," Allen said in his postgame interview with CBS.

"Looking down at these stats, man, our guys made some great plays."

Don't believe Allen. He delivered superstar stuff against the defense that was the NFL's best against the pass last year and was second-best in points allowed behind only the Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks.

Translation: Houston dominates on defense.

And Allen dominated Houston as the Bills scored the most points that defense has allowed since 2023.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

"We scored 36 points against a fantastic defense," Allen said. "However you get to 36 points in the NFL, you'll take that any other week. As long as it's more than the other guys."

Allen smiling and joking after this game is quite a different snapshot than the one we got from him in his previous game – that playoff loss to the Broncos. Allen turned the ball four times in that fateful game.

He fumbled twice, and threw two interceptions, including interception that set up the Broncos' game-winning drive.

Allen hasn't said he lost that game for the Bills, but he has taken responsibility for it. And whether he did lose it or not, the NFL narrative that Allen couldn't get his team into the Super Bowl grew.

It's impossible to make the case this was a big game on par with the playoffs. But in recording his 26th game-winning drive in the fourth quarter or overtime – the most in the league since 2018 – Allen reminded everyone that he's over that past disappointment.

And in this new season he gets another shot at the Super Bowl.

item.title: Trump unloads on AOC, Mamdani for laughing during sacred 9/11 ceremony at Ground Zero
item.description: President Donald Trump called the moment "terrible" after video showed AOC and Zohran Mamdani appearing to laugh during the Ground Zero ceremony.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump slammed Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani for appearing to laugh during the solemn reading of victims’ names at the 9/11 Memorial, calling their behavior "terrible" and "inappropriate."

"I think it’s terrible," Trump said when asked about the video of the two Democrats. "It’s not a place to be laughing, especially in that case."

"I thought it was terrible," he continued. "The fact that they were laughing together at a very important part of the ceremony was inappropriate."

The president’s condemnation came after video of Ocasio-Cortez and Mamdani sharing what appeared to be a lighthearted exchange at Ground Zero sparked widespread criticism online.

AOC, MAMDANI INTERACTION CAUGHT ON CAM AT 9/11 MEMORIAL SPARKS ONLINE FURY

A television feed from Friday’s ceremony showed a young man overcome with emotion near the memorial before cutting to Mamdani and Ocasio-Cortez smiling and appearing to laugh as they spoke. Their conversation could not be heard.

9/11 WIDOW TERRY STRADA ACCUSES US OF PROTECTING SAUDI ARABIA 25 YEARS AFTER TERROR ATTACKS, ADDRESSES VANCE

The moment unfolded as mourners read aloud the names of those killed in the Sept. 11, 2001, terrorist attacks and the 1993 World Trade Center bombing during ceremonies marking the 25th anniversary of 9/11. Nearly 3,000 people were killed in the 2001 attacks.

The video quickly spread across social media, where critics accused the pair of showing disrespect on one of the nation’s most solemn days.

MAMDANI DRAWS FURY FROM 9/11 MOURNERS OVER GROUND ZERO APPEARANCE: ‘DISRESPECTFUL’

"As the names of Americans murdered on September 11th are read aloud at Ground Zero, AOC and Mamdani are laughing and smiling together," Rep. Wesley Hunt, R-Texas, wrote on X.

"There is a time and a place for politics. This isn’t it. Ground Zero is sacred ground," Hunt added. "September 11 is not a photo op, it is not a networking event."

MAMDANI HEADS TO 9/11 MEMORIAL DESPITE 110,000-SIGNATURE PUSH FROM VICTIMS’ FAMILIES TO STAY AWAY

Meghan McCain also reacted to the video, asking on X, "Why the f--- are these two laughing?"

New York City Councilwoman Inna Vernikov, a Republican, similarly ripped the moment.

ZOHRAN MAMDANI URGED TO SKIP NEW YORK CITY'S 9/11 MEMORIAL: 'VILE ANTISEMITE'

"After thousands of families of victims of terror beg Mamdani not to show up, he stands there and laughs while families weep," Vernikov wrote. "This is NYC’s Mayor."

Mamdani had already faced opposition from some victims’ families ahead of the ceremony. A petition urging him to stay away from Ground Zero gathered more than 110,000 signatures, though Mamdani attended and remained for the ceremony.

DE NIRO CALLS CONTROVERSIAL MAMDANI POLICE COMMENTS 'RIDICULOUS' AS HE DEFENDS MAYOR GOING TO 9/11 SERVICE

However, Michael Ragusa, who has served as a member of former New York City Mayor Rudy Giuliani’s entourage, disputed claims that Mamdani and Ocasio-Cortez were joking about the ceremony.

"The videos of [them] laughing are not true. I was standing next to them the whole time," Ragusa wrote on X.

MS RACHEL DEFENDS 'AWESOME' MAMDANI AMID 9/11 MEMORIAL CONTROVERSY, SAYS HE'S VICTIM OF ISLAMOPHOBIC ATTACKS

"The camera just caught her greeting him hello," he added. "Multiple other politicians were laughing and joking behind me. Republicans and Democrats."

Mamdani was seen standing somberly at other points during the ceremony. It remains unclear what he and Ocasio-Cortez discussed during the brief exchange.

Fox News Digital previously reached out to Mamdani and Ocasio-Cortez for comment.

Fox News Digital's Charles Creitz contributed to this report.

item.title: Kyler Murray knocked out of Vikings debut after forearm to the helmet and blow to neck by two Packers
item.description: Kyler Murray left the Vikings' home opener after a brutal hit from Lukas Van Ness and Javon Bullard sent triggered the NFL concussion protocol.
item.content:encoded:
That start of Kyler Murray's career with the Minnesota Vikings has been a disaster.

That might be understating the matter.

The team's new starting quarterback threw an interception on the second play of the regular-season opener. It was his first pass in a Vikings uniform.

At home, no less.

MINNESOTA VIKINGS SURPRISINGLY DEMOTE FORMER FIRST-ROUND PICK JJ MCCARTHY TO THIRD STRING

Then Murray got knocked out of the game on his team's third possession.

Murray, signed by the Vikings in the offseason as their next major quarterback project, did not make it out of the first quarter on Sunday.

Murray left the game and underwent a concussion evaluation. He was listed officially as questionable to return, though the severity of the hit made clear to those watching that his day was over.

The Vikings eventually ruled Murray out.

Murray was scrambling when he took a forearm to the helmet from Packers defensive end Lukas Van Ness, but that wasn't all.

As Murray collapsed in a heap, he took another blow from safety Javon Bullard around the neck and head area, causing Murray's helmet to fly off.

And he seemed to go into a fencing response position, which is an involuntary body posture where an injured person extends one arm rigidly and flexes the other into the air for several seconds after a blow to the head.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

Bullard drew a personal foul for unnecessary roughness. Murray was ultimately able to walk off the field and make his way to the locker room without assistance.

Carson Wentz took over for Murray after the play, and here's the rough part:

Murray will enter the NFL concussion protocol. That means he will be tested, and independent physicians will determine when he can eventually return to play.

For a player experiencing his first concussion, the standard return-to-play timeline is roughly two weeks, though absences of one week or three weeks are not uncommon.

So, yes. It's been a terrible start to the season, and his Vikings career, for Murray.

item.title: Lions avoid franchise-worst collapse as defense stops Saints two-point conversion in OT
item.description: No Lions team had ever blown a 21-point lead, but Detroit was close to it after Tyler Shough found a rhythm in the second half in Week 1 of the NFL season.
item.content:encoded:
The Detroit Lions needed overtime and a moment of stellar defense to avoid a franchise-worst collapse against the New Orleans Saints to begin their 2026 NFL season.

What appeared to be a comfortable path to a Week 1 win became a contested, back-and-forth affair, with the Saints pushing the game to overtime after Juwan Johnson hauled in a touchdown with 1:07 remaining in the fourth quarter.

The Saints almost completed the 21-point comeback when kicker Daniel Carlson tried to knock through a 62-yard field goal at the buzzer, but he was wide right to force the first overtime game of the new campaign.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

But just like it was in the second half, the Lions and Saints both traded touchdowns, as Amon-Ra St. Brown scored to open up the extra period, while tight end Noah Fant caught one on the other side of the field on the ensuing drive.

The difference? New Orleans head coach Kellen Moore didn’t feel like tying the score anymore. He was going for the win with a two-point conversion.

After an 80-yard drive, the Saints wanted to walk it off with the victory, but the Lions’ defense came through when they needed it most. A three-man stack of receivers broke off for the Saints when the ball was snapped and quarterback Tyler Shough threw it up for rookie Bryce Lance, but the pass was broken up to the delight of everyone inside Ford Field in Detroit.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

The Lions celebrated their hard-fought victory, but it shouldn’t have been that close if you ask them.

If Detroit lost, their 21-point lead would’ve been the biggest in franchise history that they gave up in a defeat. So, this group, which has high hopes out of the NFC North this season, is happy not to be on the wrong side of history.

Things were going well for the Lions until Shough and company, who struggled throughout most of the game, finally got on the scoreboard in the third quarter with a touchdown by running back Kendre Miller. From there, the Saints put together three more scoring drives, including a touchdown grab by Devaughn Vele and a field goal from Carlson.

The Lions will hope to clean up things defensively, but offensively, it’s clear as day what Jahmyr Gibbs can do, especially with an extra workload, now that David Montgomery is no longer in Detroit.

The star running back finished the game with 156 yards rushing with two scores on the ground, while hauling in five of Jared Goff’s passes for 30 yards. Gibbs turned 34 touches into 186 scrimmage yards, and that’s what many are expecting each week from one of the most explosive and dynamic offensive weapons in the sport each week.

Meanwhile, Shough threw for 410 yards on 35-of-56 through the air, though he was intercepted twice by the Lions’ defense. Chris Olave, his top target, finished the game with 10 catches for 182 yards.

item.title: Hayden Panettiere's boyfriend Brian Hickerson involved in bloody bar altercation weeks after star's death
item.description: Video shows a handcuffed and bloody Brian Hickerson at Wild Wing Café in Greenville, South Carolina, just weeks after Hayden Panettiere's death.
item.content:encoded:
Hayden Panettiere’s boyfriend Brian Hickerson was involved in a bar altercation just weeks after the late actress' sudden death.

On Sept. 12 at approximately 9:10 p.m., officers were dispatched to Wild Wing Café in South Carolina after receiving a report of an assault inside the restaurant, according to a statement from the Greenville Police Department obtained by Fox News Digital.

"Upon arrival, officers located several individuals involved in an altercation and detained multiple patrons while the incident was investigated," police said.

HAYDEN PANETTIERE’S BOYFRIEND’S BROTHER REVEALS WHAT HAPPENED INSIDE AIRBNB BEFORE ACTRESS'S DEATH

Two of the individuals were identified as Hickerson and his brother, Zachary Hickerson.

Police said Zachary was "highly intoxicated" during the incident and began yelling profanities in a public setting. He was taken into custody on a disorderly conduct charge and transported to the Greenville County Detention Center.

HAYDEN PANETTIERE’S REP SLAMS ‘GOSSIP AND SPECULATION’ AS DEATH INVESTIGATION DEEPENS

In a video circulating online, Hickerson — who was seen handcuffed and bloody outside the restaurant - told Zachary, "GPD leaked it when my girlfriend died," referencing Panettiere's death and the Greenville Police Department.

In another video obtained by TMZ, Hickerson is seen throwing a bar stool before eventually getting carried out of the establishment.

Hickerson was later released from the scene and was not charged, GPD said.

HAYDEN PANETTIERE’S MOM DISCLOSES HEARTBREAKING ULTIMATUM IN THEIR FINAL PHONE CALL BEFORE ACTRESS’ DEATH

Representatives for Hickerson and Zachary did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital’s request for comment.

The incident comes less than a month after Panettiere, Hickerson’s on-again, off-again girlfriend, was found dead inside a Greenville residence on Aug. 16. She was 36.

Hickerson and his brother, Zach, called 911 after finding the actress unresponsive, according to a police report obtained by Fox News Digital. Hickerson later gave authorities a bag containing medication Panettiere had been taking, according to the report.

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

The police report claimed Zach appeared "very emotional" while paramedics worked to revive Panettiere. Meanwhile, Hickerson did not become emotional until the "Ice Princess" star was declared deceased.

Officers were also given a bag of medication Panettiere had allegedly been taking by Hickerson.

Hickerson reportedly traveled with the "Remember the Titans" actress from Los Angeles the day before she was found unresponsive at a Greenville, South Carolina, apartment complex on Aug. 16, according to TMZ. The two broke up briefly in 2022, but rekindled their romance the following year. Hickerson's brother confirmed to police Brian was in a relationship with the actress at the time of Panettiere's death.

Preliminary autopsy results found no signs of trauma that contributed to Panettiere’s death, the Greenville County Coroner's Office confirmed to Fox News Digital. However, Panettiere's death remains under investigation.

HAYDEN PANETTIERE REMEMBERED BY VIOLA DAVIS, BETHANY JOY LENZ AND OTHER CELEBRITIES AFTER SUDDEN DEATH AT 36

Fox News has learned the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) has also been contacted and is assisting with the investigation.

Shortly after her death, Panettiere's mom, Lesley Vogel, opened up about her daughter's final months during an interview with "Good Morning America."

One day later, Panettiere's representatives condemned the speculation surrounding Panettiere’s final hours and accused outsiders of turning her death into an opportunity to "fuel gossip."

"Many people who were not close to Hayden are using her death as an opportunity to fuel gossip and speculation about a situation they knew very little about," Panettiere's rep said in a statement shared with US Weekly. "It is deeply disrespectful to her memory and to those who knew and loved her and are actively grieving this tremendous loss."

WLADIMIR KLITSCHKO MOURNS FORMER FIANCÉE HAYDEN PANETTIERE, VOWS TO KEEP HER MEMORY ALIVE FOR DAUGHTER KAYA

"If you have legitimate information that could be helpful, please contact law enforcement rather than turning to social media to speculate publicly about something you do not fully understand."

Panettiere's team also hinted that key details surrounding Panettiere’s death had yet to emerge.

"There is much more to this story than what is currently being discussed publicly, and those closest to Hayden are actively cooperating with the ongoing investigation to help ensure that the truth comes to light and that justice is properly served," the statement concluded.

Fox News Digital's Lauryn Overhultz and Tracy Wright contributed to this post.

item.title: Hasan Piker doubles down, defends his 'God-given right' to say how much he hates America
item.description: Hasan Piker defended his right to say he hates America on his Twitch livestream after an attack ad tied his rhetoric to Abdul El-Sayed's Michigan Senate race.
item.content:encoded:
Far-left Twitch streamer Hasan Piker insisted it was his "God-given" and "constitutionally protected right" to proclaim hatred for America on his livestream Friday.

During one of his lengthy shows, Piker responded to an attack ad against Democratic Michigan U.S. Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed based on his connection to Piker and his past controversial statements claiming to "hate" America.

"Bro, I hate this country, dude. I hate America," Piker said in clips featured on the ad. "Oh God, I f---ing hate America so much."

WHO IS HASAN PIKER? MEET THE FAR-LEFT STREAMER WHO IS STIRRING UP CONTROVERSY AND DIVIDING DEMOCRATS

On his Friday livestream, Piker argued that it was "clear" that he was angry at "what America as the American government is doing to Americans and to everyone else" but nevertheless defended his right to say he hates the country.

"Of course I'm a God---- American. It is my God---- God-given and constitutionally protected right to say I hate America if America is actually f---ing over Americans. You can clip chimp it all day. It doesn't change that. It doesn't change that mentality. To present this as like, oh, 'these guys are real America haters' as some liberals have been doing on the timeline, as virtually the entirety of the Republican Party is doing is so f---ing stupid," Piker said.

EL-SAYED DISAVOWS HASAN PIKER'S 9/11 COMMENTS BUT DECRIES 'CANCEL CULTURE'

He continued, "How can you not get angry and resentful about a government that does nothing to treat its sickly, to feed its hungry, to feed its starving, to shelter its homeless, when we have all the money we have an abundance of wealth and prosperity, and we just refuse to spread it around? Of course that makes me f---ing angry. It's shocking to me that you act as though it doesn't make you angry at all."

Fox News Digital reached out to Piker for comment.

HASAN PIKER DRAWS FRESH SCRUTINY AFTER FRAMING NEWSPAPER COVERING 9/11 ATTACKS IN STREAM BACKGROUND

El-Sayed has faced backlash for campaigning with Piker during the primary election, even after Piker was being criticized for claiming America "deserved" 9/11. The Michigan Democrat has since distanced himself from Piker in recent weeks as he campaigns in the general election.

Piker himself has acknowledged his extreme language. In an exclusive interview at the 2026 Socialism Conference in Chicago last week, Piker defended his comments as attacking America's "meddling in the affairs in the Middle East," but admitted that he should not have used the word "deserved."

"It's not a controversial thing [to argue]," Piker said to Fox News Digital. "It was the language that I used that was controversial."

item.title: Mike Johnson rejects AI moratorium over China threat as conservative activist demands guardrails
item.description: House Speaker Mike Johnson rejected an AI moratorium, warning China could overtake the U.S. as Anthropic, Elon Musk and Sam Altman push for a slowdown.
item.content:encoded:
House Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., rejected an emergency moratorium on artificial intelligence development Sunday during CNN's "State of the Union," warning that slowing American innovation could allow China to pull ahead as tech executives and lawmakers intensify calls for new AI safety measures.

"We have to resist Congress jumping in and imposing some sort of emergency moratorium," Johnson said. "Here's what I'm proposing: I think the leaders and providers of these platforms need to come together in a meeting with us and figure out what the right balance is. We cannot put a moratorium on this because China will overlap us."

Republican National Committee member and Humans First chairwoman Amy Kremer told Fox News Digital on Sunday that policymakers should pursue safeguards without surrendering America's technological advantage to Beijing.

"We need guardrails that protect Americans while allowing American innovation to lead the world," Kremer said. "That means protecting children, workers and our national security, while making sure China doesn't win the AI race."

AI KILL SWITCH BILL COULD SHUT DOWN ROGUE MODELS

Kremer, who has emerged as a prominent Republican critic of the rapid expansion of AI data centers, also said Congress should preserve state and local authority over the infrastructure needed to power the technology. 

Humans First, a grassroots conservative movement against new data centers, is pushing a policy framework that opposes blanket data-center moratoriums while calling for local control and rejecting eminent domain for projects.

"When it comes to the massive data centers being built to power AI, Washington should not strip states and local communities of their authority," Kremer said.

"The people who live with these projects should have a voice in whether and where they're built. They also have a right to know who that company is before decisions are made, not after the deal is done," she added.

The AI debate accelerated after Anthrophic CEO Dario Amodei called Saturday for slowing the development of increasingly capable AI models, drawing support from xAI founder Elon Musk and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman.

SEN. BERNIE SANDERS: YES, WE MUST HIT THE PAUSE BUTTON ON AI BEFORE IT IS TOO LATE

"We must slow the pace at which we improve the capabilities of AI models. Progress will still seem fast, and we must make wise use of the time we gain," Amodei said.

President Donald Trump rejected calls for a broader slowdown Sunday while speaking to reporters in Ireland, placing the emerging technology in the context of U.S. competition with China.

"We’re leading China on AI. We’re the most sophisticated country in the world and, frankly, I want to keep it that way, because whoever wins AI wins," Trump said.

Public concern has also centered on the infrastructure required to sustain AI growth. A July Fox News poll found 70% of registered voters opposed construction of AI data centers in their area, while 30% supported them.

FOX NEWS POLL: COOL YOUR SERVERS! VOTERS REJECT DATA CENTERS

The Trump administration has sought to address concerns about electricity costs through its Ratepayer Protection Pledge, which requires participating AI companies and data-center operators to cover the power-generation and infrastructure costs associated with their facilities rather than passing them to customers. The White House says the pledge now covers roughly 80% of electricity delivered to American homes and businesses.

Kremer told Fox News Digital that protecting consumers should extend beyond electricity prices.

"Americans shouldn't be forced to subsidize Big Tech through higher electricity bills, tax giveaways, eminent domain or the loss of productive farmland," Kremer said.

Johnson said he wants the major AI executives brought together with policymakers to work through the competing national security and safety concerns, suggesting the White House could host the talks.

"We’ve got to summon everybody together," Johnson said. "They probably should be summoned together at the White House. And I think we need to go in a big room, close the door and sort this out. And I’ll be the one pushing for it."

item.title: GOP gov candidate recounts miracle water landing as dispatch audio reveals desperate search for sinking plane
item.description: Dispatch audio captures the frantic search for Tom Tiffany after his plane lost power and plunged into Lake Wausau in darkness Saturday night.
item.content:encoded:
A desperate search unfolded across a dark Wisconsin lake after Republican gubernatorial candidate Tom Tiffany’s powerless plane plunged into the water and disappeared beneath the surface with rescuers unsure where he and his pilot had gone.

Dramatic dispatch audio captures crews calling for more ambulances, engines and boats as they raced to find the two men and tracked the last GPS location of a phone believed to be underwater.

"We’re going to be in search for a down plane," one responder warned.

WISCONSIN GOP GOVERNOR CANDIDATE SWIMS FROM SINKING PLANE AFTER EMERGENCY LAKE LANDING

Hours after leaving the hospital, Tiffany revealed Sunday that pilot Leonard "Len" Boltz had just seconds to react after the plane lost power on its final approach to Wausau Downtown Airport.

"Len said to me, ‘We are going down. Pull your seatbelt tight,’" Tiffany recalled during a news conference. "And that’s exactly what I did. I gave it a yank and pulled it good and tight."

COAST GUARD PLANE WITH DHS SECRETARY MARKWAYNE MULLIN ON BOARD MAKES EMERGENCY LANDING AFTER ENGINE FAILURE

"It was probably about 10 seconds later," he added. "We hit the water."

The impact sent Tiffany’s head into the dashboard, leaving him with a gash above his right eye that required 12 stitches. Boltz received four stitches for one of his injuries, Tiffany said.

PILOT'S BRAVERY ON DISPLAY IN STEERING CRIPPLED PLANE CLEAR OF TRAGEDY IN DRAMATIC WATER LANDING

The two men checked on each other before escaping through the passenger-side door as the plane began filling with water.

Tiffany searched the cockpit for his phone but could not find it. Boltz still had his phone and called 911.

PILOT DECLARES MAYDAY BEFORE SEAPLANE COMES DOWN IN NEW YORK CITY’S EAST RIVER

They climbed atop the slowly sinking plane and waited there for roughly 10 minutes as emergency lights appeared around the lake.

As the aircraft slipped underwater beneath them, they began swimming toward the airport. They made it roughly 100 to 150 feet before Tiffany reached a high spot in the lake where the water was about five feet deep.

MULTIPLE INJURED AFTER FLOATPLANE MAKES EMERGENCY LANDING, CATCHES FIRE OFF WASHINGTON COAST

"I said to Len, ‘Let’s just stay right here until help can come,’ because we could see the sirens," Tiffany said.

His voice cracked as the gravity of the ordeal appeared to catch up with him.

"We are just really fortunate," Tiffany said, pausing as he became emotional. "We’re really fortunate that God was looking after us last night."

The dispatch audio revealed the uncertainty confronting first responders as they raced toward different points along Lake Wausau.

"Can you get another ambulance rolling this way and one more engine, please?" one responder said. "Also page SAFER mutual aid to Bluegill Park with a boat."

Another responder reported that a witness had seen the aircraft go down but could provide only a general search area.

"I’m on scene with the reporting party," the responder said. "He stated he did see [an] aircraft crash."

4 FLORIDA FAMILY MEMBERS FOUND DEAD AFTER SMALL PLANE GOES DOWN OFF THE BAHAMAS

Crews carried thermal-imaging equipment and used a phone’s last known GPS coordinates to narrow the search. A landowner also provided a boat for deputies to use, according to the radio traffic.

"I was talking to the pilots," a responder said. "It sounds like they may plan to swim to the nearest shore after it went under, and then I lost contact with them."

"I believe his phone is underwater," he added. "They may be swimming south, I believe."

The tense search ended when rescuers announced that both men had been located.

"We have two victims in the water," a responder said. "We’re just pulling them out now."

Minutes later, a crew reported both were "alert, conscious" and confirmed everyone aboard the aircraft had been accounted for.

Tiffany credited Boltz’s experience with keeping the emergency landing from becoming deadly. The former Air Force pilot trainer raised the plane’s landing gear before touching down, preventing it from potentially cartwheeling across the water.

"He was savvy enough and quick enough to think about, ‘We’ve got to make sure and pull that landing gear up,’" Tiffany said. "He did that, and it might have saved us."

Tiffany estimated the plane was still traveling between 70 and 80 mph when it hit the lake, describing the impact as "a fast-moving car crash."

"We’re fortunate the plane didn’t flip," he said. "I just take that to the skill of the pilot."

Wausau Mayor Doug Diny, a former military pilot, also praised Boltz for safely bringing the aircraft down at night.

PILOT RESCUED AFTER WORLD WAR II-ERA PLANE CRASHES AT PENNSYLVANIA AIRPORT

"The last thing anyone wants to do as a pilot is put the aircraft in the water at night," Diny said.

Tiffany and Boltz were taken to Aspirus Wausau Hospital and released after treatment. Tiffany said a CT scan found no apparent concussion, though doctors instructed him to watch for possible symptoms and avoid flying for several days.

Despite canceling a trip to Washington, D.C., Tiffany said he plans to return to the campaign trail Monday.

"This will not deter me in my efforts that I started a year ago to become the next governor of the state of Wisconsin," he said.

The single-engine Beechcraft Bonanza remained submerged Sunday. The Federal Aviation Administration is investigating what caused it to lose power.

House Speaker Mike Johnson celebrated Tiffany’s return following the close call.

"Grateful to God no one was hurt in this accident and my good friend @TomTiffanyWI is safe and back on the trail!" Johnson wrote on X.

Tiffany represents Wisconsin’s 7th Congressional District and is running against Democratic Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley in November.

Crowley said he was grateful Tiffany and the pilot survived and praised Boltz’s actions.

item.title: Ms. Rachel claims celebrities silent on Gaza would ‘probably’ speak if children ‘were White’
item.description: Children's YouTuber Ms. Rachel accused silent celebrities of racism over Palestinian children killed in Gaza, claiming a racial double standard.
item.content:encoded:
Children's YouTuber star Ms. Rachel accused celebrities and leaders of racism on Saturday for remaining silent about Palestinian children killed in Gaza, claiming the lack of public advocacy reflected a racial double standard in how children's lives are valued.

Ms. Rachel, whose real name is Rachel Griffin Accurso, directly accused those who have not spoken publicly about the war of treating Palestinian children differently because of their race.

"They probably would say something if these kids were White and from a different place. Please stop being racist and risk something," Accurso said on Instagram.

CHILDREN'S YOUTUBE STAR 'MS. RACHEL' STIRS CONTROVERSY WITH RACIAL CLAIM ABOUT NOLAN WELLS INVESTIGATION

The accusation came less than two weeks after podcaster Avi Lichtschein confronted Accurso over her repeated characterization of Israel's war against Hamas as a "genocide." 

Lichtschein told Fox News Digital that even if Accurso's advocacy comes from concern for children, her enormous platform requires her to consider the impact of the rhetoric she promotes.

"When you have an audience as enormous as hers, you have a responsibility to understand the consequences of the claims you’re amplifying," Lichtschein said.

Accurso divided celebrities and leaders into two groups: those willing to speak publicly about Palestinian children and those she claimed were deliberately remaining silent because they placed less value on their lives.

"Those who are willing to shout at the top of their lungs that over 20,000 Palestinian children shouldn’t have been killed in the Gaza genocide and those that remain silent because these children are not worth it to them," Accurso said. "I see that you have a hierarchy of children’s lives."

UNICEF GAZA FINDINGS ‘COMPLETELY SHATTERS’ STARVATION CLAIMS AGAINST ISRAEL, STATE DEPT SAYS

A June report from the United Nations' Independent International Commission of Inquiry said at least 20,179 Palestinian children had been killed and 44,143 injured between the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas attacks and the commission's reporting period through March 31. 

The commission accused Israeli forces of deliberately targeting children and concluded the conduct formed part of what it characterized as genocide.

The commission's previous findings also documented Hamas' treatment of Israeli children on Oct. 7, saying 40 Israeli children were killed, hundreds were injured and children were deliberately abducted during the terrorist attack.

Israel has rejected the commission's findings and its methodology. In its formal response to the June report, the Israeli government said the commission's composition, mandate and methodology were fundamentally flawed and accused the document of containing extensive errors and omissions.

ANTISEMITIC VIOLENCE REACHES DEADLIEST LEVEL SINCE 1994, NEW GLOBAL REPORT FINDS

Accurso has faced increasing scrutiny over her Israel-related activism. 

Fox News Digital reported in January that Accurso appeared to like an Instagram comment reading, "Free America from the Jews." Accurso apologized and said she accidentally liked the comment while attempting to delete it.

In a statement provided directly to Fox News Digital after that controversy, Accurso rejected antisemitism and maintained that her advocacy was rooted in concern for people regardless of background.

"Antisemitism and hate of any kind have no place in my life or my work," Accurso said.

Accurso previously said she was "horrified by October 7" and rejected accusations that her advocacy for Palestinian children meant she cared less about Israeli children. 

Last month, during her encounter with Lichtschein, she maintained that she was not anti-Israel and described her opposition as directed at the Israeli government and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

Elizabeth Barcohana, the California Republican Party’s Jewish engagement chair told Fox News Digital on Sunday that Ms. Rachel's outrage was "fake" and selective, while also saying the children's educator was "sanitizing terrorism."

"The source of her figure of 20,000 child deaths comes directly from the 'Gaza Ministry of Health,' which is Hamas itself, meaning, Ms. Rachel has appointed herself to be a mouthpiece for a terrorist organization," she added. "Further, the figure does not distinguish between innocent children and the minor male teens we know fight for Hamas and Palestinian Islamic Jihad; nor does it distinguish deaths caused by Israeli strikes in which there were human-shield civilian casualties from Palestinian rockets, Hamas/PIJ explosives, friendly fire, or other internal violence."

"Ms. Rachel is essentially sanitizing terrorism with false and misleading information to emotionally manipulate her very impressionable following and those around her in her industry. This is very dangerous, and every mother whose child watches Ms. Rachel videos must be made aware of who she really is," Barcohana said.

Fox News Digital reached out to the Anti-Defamation League and Jewish Federations of North America for comment, but did not immediately receive a response.

item.title: Chick-fil-A is one of America's toughest franchises, and the startup cost may shock you
item.description: Julian Good reveals Chick-fil-A's $10,000 franchise fee and the staggering odds facing 100,000 yearly applicants vying for roughly 200 spots.
item.content:encoded:
Chick-fil-A is one of America's toughest franchises to get, attracting thousands of hopeful applicants each year for a limited number of owner-operator opportunities.

The fast-food chain's unique business model was recently highlighted by Julian Good, who owns a Chick-fil-A restaurant in St. Charles, Illinois, during an appearance on the "Founder Talk" podcast.

"It's a $10,000 franchise fee. It's been the same for the last 50 years," Good said.

CHICK-FIL-A COPYCAT RECIPE REVEALED AS CEO SHARES INGREDIENT THAT MAKES IT TASTE LIKE THE ORIGINAL

About 100,000 people apply each year to become a Chick-fil-A owner-operator, with roughly 200 ultimately selected, Good explained.

Applicants without Chick-fil-A experience often wait three to five years before receiving an opportunity, he added.

Chick-fil-A describes its selection process as "highly competitive," saying it looks for leaders willing to devote their full time and best efforts to operating a restaurant, according to Chick-fil-A’s January 2024 post on its press room website.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

However, previous experience with the company isn't required.

More than 25% of newly selected owner-operators had never worked at one of its restaurants or for the company before applying, according to Chick-fil-A.

The company said operators also come from a wide range of professional backgrounds, including manufacturing, health care, education, law enforcement and retail.

Unlike many franchise systems, Chick-fil-A owner-operators do not own the restaurant they operate, according to Franchise Business Review. Chick-fil-A retains ownership of the restaurant, equipment and, in most cases, the real estate, meaning operators do not build equity in the business or sell it when they retire.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES

Chick-fil-A said operators devote their time and energy to managing their restaurants, developing employees and serving their communities.

Good said that's one of the biggest differences between Chick-fil-A and many competing franchise models.

"When a Chick-fil-A operator retires, you can't pass it down to your kids. You don't sell the business or anything. It just goes back into the hands of Chick-fil-A," he said.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Chick-fil-A's unique approach also extends to its operating schedule, with all of its restaurants closed on Sundays.

The weekly tradition remains an important part of the company's culture, Good noted.

"Just a way to glorify God and give back to the team and the community," he said.

Fox News Digital reached out to Chick-fil-A for comment.

item.title: Trump says Lindsay Clancy case is a ‘state situation' following attorney's pardon plea
item.description: President Donald Trump expressed sympathy for the family of Lindsay Clancy’s three children while signaling that he would not intervene in the former nurse’s state murder case.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump on Sunday signaled that he would not intervene in the case of Massachusetts mother Lindsay Clancy, who is charged with killing her three young children amid allegations that she suffered from postpartum psychosis. 

When asked whether he would pardon Clancy, Trump called the situation "very sad" but said the case is ultimately a "state situation," not a federal one.

"There’s no winner there. There’s no win no matter what you do. Three children are dead," he said. 

LINDSAY CLANCY'S LAWYER REVEALS POST-MISTRIAL STRATEGY AS RETRIAL LOOMS

The response came after Kevin Reddington, who represents Clancy, publicly asked Trump to grant his client a pardon last week. Reddington had acknowledged that Trump had no authority to issue a pardon in a state matter, but hoped he could still influence the outcome, according to his interview with WBZ-TV. 

Trump indicated that the defense and prosecution need to resolve the legal matter at the local level while praising Reddington's work. 

"He’s a good attorney. I’ve heard from other people he’s a very good attorney," Trump said. "I hope they can work it out. That’s something they have to work out … There is no win there."

LINDSAY CLANCY JUROR ADMITTED 'REASONABLE DOUBT' BUT STILL REFUSED INSANITY VERDICT, FOREPERSON SAYS

Previously, Trump said Clancy would still have to "pay the price" for the deaths of her three children. 

"I assume there's going to be another trial. It's a terrible situation. Look, she did a horrible, horrible thing. Can't be worse. But you'll find out what the price to pay is. There'll be a price. It's going to be [a] mental institution or jail or something," he said. 

Clancy, a 36-year-old former nurse, faces three counts of first-degree murder in the 2023 deaths of her children: 5-year-old Cora, 3-year-old Dawson and 8-month-old Callan. 

After their deaths, Clancy attempted to kill herself and was left paralyzed from the injuries. 

Her defense attorneys have argued that Clancy suffered from postpartum psychosis, a severe but rare psychiatric condition that causes a sudden loss of reality after childbirth. 

According to ABC, Reddington said Clancy had sought treatment from a psychiatrist he described as inexperienced. The psychiatrist reportedly prescribed her medications for postpartum depression in the months leading up to her reported psychotic break. 

Clancy now faces a potential retrial after jurors deadlocked following a full week of deliberations, prompting Judge William Sullivan to declare a mistrial earlier this month. 

The jury was split 11 to 1, with 11 jurors reportedly favoring an acquittal on the grounds that Clancy was not criminally responsible for the killings. The jury consisted of nine women and three men.  

Fox News Digital’s Michael Ruiz and Elaine Mallon contributed to this report.

item.title: Joanna Gaines reveals why she and Chip walked away from 'Fixer Upper' at the height of its success
item.description: Joanna Gaines described a deep "soul weariness" that led her and Chip Gaines to walk away from "Fixer Upper" despite pressure to keep going.
item.content:encoded:
Joanna Gaines had success knocking on every door — and she decided to stop answering.

At the height of "Fixer Upper" fame, the home design and lifestyle expert and her husband, Chip Gaines, walked away from the nonstop grind despite pressure from their representatives to keep going.

Years later, Joanna explained that she had reached a point where she was experiencing what she called "soul weariness."

JOANNA GAINES KEEPS LIFE SIMPLE IN TEXAS AWAY FROM HOLLYWOOD SPOTLIGHT

"When you start realizing you're living on a thing that's now… the intentionality is gone, and you're just showing up… that doesn't feel fulfilling," she said on the "Joy 101 with Hoda Kotb" podcast. "It actually feels as though we're part of this machine that is like, 'What's the life here?'"

She added, "I would say that was our first pause of like, ‘We're doing all this and seeing great reward … this is wonderful,’ but also never at the expense of … our like livelihood, our happiness, our souls."

That pause would become a blueprint for how Joanna thinks about work — and burnout — today.

"Stopping in that moment was basically us saying … ‘What's worth it is, like are we healthy? Are we good? Is our family good?’ That's the most important thing. So that was really a very pivotal moment for us."

"Fixer Upper" turned Chip and Joanna into television stars, but even as the HGTV hit reached new heights, the couple knew they couldn't keep running at full speed forever.

The Gaines’s first stepped in front of television cameras when the "Fixer Upper" pilot aired in 2013. The series followed the husband-and-wife duo as they took on rundown homes in Waco, Texas, and transformed them into polished spaces for their clients — all while growing their increasingly influential Magnolia brand.

The show quickly became a hit, making Joanna and Chip familiar faces far beyond the world of home renovation.

COUNTRY STAR STEPS AWAY FROM MUSIC TO FOCUS ON HIMSELF AFTER FAME TOOK A TOLL

In September 2017, the couple announced they would end "Fixer Upper" after its fifth season, choosing to step away while the series was still riding high.

Joanna said she and Chip have spent almost 25 years building their business. But about three years ago, she said, they stopped seeing where they were headed.

"We stopped seeing vision. We stopped remembering, ‘Like why are we doing this?’"

The couple decided to take the summer off.

KATHIE LEE GIFFORD ADMITS SHE 'WANTED TO DIE' AFTER MISDIAGNOSIS AND MULTIPLE SURGERIES FOR CHRONIC PAIN

However, the decision wasn't consequence-free. 

Joanna acknowledged that stepping away meant putting pressure on their team.

"Which meant disappointing our team, disappointing a lot of things … So it cost us something. It cost people something."

"But that three months was time for us to go, ‘We need a break. We need clarity. Why are we building this? What are we doing this for?’"

Joanna remembered the moment she felt the burnout was impossible to ignore.

"When you start dreading your days, like ‘I don't want to do that.’"

For Gaines, that sense of dread eventually became so pronounced that she found herself looking for almost any excuse to hit pause — even an unexpected illness.

"You start like wishing for a stomach bug or … 'Okay, maybe back surgery this year would be great.’ Like how do I force myself?" she laughed.

'80S POP STAR TIFFANY EMBRACES QUIET NASHVILLE ROUTINE AFTER LEAVING CALIFORNIA BEHIND FOR GOOD

Physical exhaustion, Joanna explained, is something she knows how to push through.

But the deeper exhaustion is different, she argued.

"So there's that part, but also just … where your soul just feels weary."

She described the "soul" as the deeper part of a person — the place that can run dry even when the body is still capable of performing.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"From a physical standpoint, I can work till I can … I can push past the weariness the physical, but then you get to that layer of like the soul weariness and that's dangerous."

Joanna said that was the warning she is now determined not to ignore, describing the feeling as a "holy fear."

For the entrepreneur and television personality who built an empire by constantly creating, the hardest lesson may have been learning that she cannot simply outwork exhaustion.

The Magnolia Network stars tied the knot in 2003. Joanna and Chip are parents to five children — Ella, Drake, Crew, Emmie and Duke.

As the Gaines’s planted their roots in Waco, Texas, their Magnolia businesses took off.

After five seasons of "Fixer Upper," the original series ended in 2018. Magnolia Network programming later debuted on Discovery+ in 2021 before the linear Magnolia Network replaced DIY Network in January 2022.

The couple's Magnolia Market at the Silos in Waco includes Magnolia Market, the Shops at the Silos, Silos Baking Co. and Magnolia Press Coffee Co. They also operate Magnolia Table elsewhere in Waco.

The design duo additionally publish "Magnolia Journal" and have written a series of lifestyle books. They have a Magnolia Home furniture and accessories collection, and Joanna created the Hearth & Hand with Magnolia collection for Target.

Chip and Joanna also opened the 33-room Hotel 1928 in Waco in 2023 after renovating a historic building in partnership with AJ Capital. The couple also offers Magnolia vacation rentals in Waco.

item.title: Homan confirms 'criminal' investigation involving Ilhan Omar, says he knows 'things are going on’
item.description: Tom Homan confirmed officials are investigating allegations involving Rep. Ilhan Omar but declined to share specifics about possible immigration fraud.
item.content:encoded:
White House border czar Tom Homan confirmed on "The Sunday Briefing" that the Department of Homeland Security is looking into allegations involving Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., but would not disclose details about what he described as an "ongoing criminal investigation."

Pressed on whether the federal government has evidence that Omar committed immigration or naturalization fraud, Homan declined to comment.

"I know things are going on, but I can't give specifics of what's happening," Homan said.

"If someone committed an immigration violation, if someone committed marriage fraud or anything like that, regardless if they're a congressman or not, no one's above the law. So, I'll leave it at that. We'll let HSI, Homeland Security Investigations, continue the investigation."

FEDS SAY RAPE CONVICT LIED HIS WAY INTO US CITIZENSHIP BY HIDING SEX ASSAULTS

When subsequently asked directly whether he was confirming an investigation involving Omar, Homan replied, "I'm confirming that ICE is, yeah — look, I said months ago that there's something that's been reported and needs to be looked at."

Omar has long been dogged by allegations that she married a man that critics allege is her brother as part of an immigration scheme. Omar has repeatedly denied the allegation, and the claim has not been proven in public records. In December, she dismissed the claims as "bigoted lies," writing on social media that Trump was obsessed with her.

Homan's comments follow Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Secretary Markwayne Mullin's appearance on a podcast, during which he said, "Something's going to happen. ... We know that she married her brother to try to bring him to the United States. We know he now lives in London.

ILHAN OMAR LASHES OUT AT 'SICK' REPUBLICANS FOR INVESTIGATING HER ALLEGED MARRIAGE TO BROTHER

"There may be more to this, the whole family migration and possibly some illegal activity for them to come to the United States to begin with. ... If we can prove it, that you shouldn't have been here in the first place, we will deport you."

Homan did not disclose any information about possible evidence or charges.

'SQUAD' DEM DISMISSES FRAUD PROBE SPECULATION AFTER $29M NET-WORTH DROP

Vice President JD Vance said in May that the Justice Department was looking into whether Omar committed immigration fraud.

"You read the things about Ilhan Omar … who she married and whether she didn't marry this person or that person," Vance said then. "It certainly seems like something fishy is there, but everybody's entitled to equal justice under the law."

The vice president's comments follow his own podcast interview in March, during which he told conservative commentator Benny Johnson he had spoken with White House immigration advisor Stephen Miller about potential legal action against Omar.

"We think Ilhan Omar definitely committed immigration fraud against the United States of America," Vance said at the time.

There is a denaturalization process for cases of proven immigration fraud, Homan said, characterizing it as "very serious."

"If someone lies through that process to becoming a citizen, and we can prove they, in fact, lied or misrepresented themselves, we can absolutely denaturalize them. We've done it before many times over the last 40 years I've been around, so it's a process," he said.

Fox News Digital reached out to Omar's office for comment.

Fox News Digital's Louis Casiano contributed to this report.

item.title: Breanna Stewart's double-double, Caitlin Clark's emergence off bench help US to World Cup win over France
item.description: Team USA won its fifth consecutive FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup tournament on Sunday with a dominating victory against France in Germany.
item.content:encoded:
Team USA women’s basketball remained dominant on the world stage on Sunday.

Breanna Stewart, Jackie Young and Caitlin Clark’s emergence off the bench propelled the Americans to a gold-medal victory over France, 97-79. It is Team USA’s fifth consecutive gold medal in the FIBA Women’s Basketball World Cup and seventh in the last eight tournaments.

The U.S. had to fight and claw its way back into the game after trailing in the first half. But they outscored France 30-12 in the third quarter and used the run to help solidify the victory.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Stewart had a double-double to finish off the French. She scored 22 points and grabbed 10 rebounds. The New York Liberty star’s presence on the interior proved to be a game-changer. She was plus-8 on the floor and shot 70% from the field. She was named MVP of the tournament.

Jackie Young added 18 points, six rebounds and five assists. Young was plus-15 on the floor and shot 50% from the field. She was named the player of the game.

Clark played about 12 minutes off the bench but provided some key buckets for the Americans. She made a buzzer-beating shot before halftime to cut the deficit to two points. As the U.S. continued to surge into the fourth quarter, Clark hit a big 3-pointer to put France on its heels.

She finished with 12 points and three assists.

Though Clark wasn’t a starter in the USA lineup, her presence on the floor in key moments of the game appeared to be fruitful. While the starters needed a breather after getting back into the game, Clark and the rest of her teammates off the bench helped provide the necessary scoring to keep France at bay.

France started out hot.

The duo of Dominique Malonga and Gabby Williams proved to be a formidable force for the Americans to deal with. Malonga scored 21 points to lead France, while Williams added 20 of her own. France didn’t get any other player into double figures. Valeriane Ayayi was the closest as she scored eight points in 26 minutes.

France only made four field goals in the third quarter and the cold streak allowed the U.S. to take the lead and pull away from there.

It is now 12 gold medals in total for the U.S. as they have remained dominant no matter which global tournament they enter.

France may have been the biggest challenge to the U.S. reign as they only lost by one to them in the gold medal game at the 2024 Summer Olympics. But the emergence of young stars like Clark, Paige Bueckers and Angel Reese helped keep the Americans at the top of the food chain throughout the tournament.

The players will take a moment to celebrate the achievement but in a few days, it’s back to the WNBA where the playoffs are on the horizon.

item.title: Nick Saban wants a different criteria for judging which teams reach the College Football Playoff
item.description: Nick Saban urged a strength of schedule overhaul on "College GameDay" before Oregon's shocking upset and Texas' fourth quarter comeback over Ohio State.
item.content:encoded:
If you thought Week 1 of the college football season was wild, Week 2 took the typical chaos to a whole new level.

Out of nowhere, the Oregon Ducks suffered a shocking upset on the road to the recently hapless Oklahoma State Cowboys. The Michigan Wolverines, who dropped out of the Top 25 after a disappointing "win" over Western Michigan, and seemed eliminated from contention for the College Football Playoff, beat the No. 11 Oklahoma Sooners.

The game of the week delivered, in spades, with the Texas Longhorns completing a remarkable fourth quarter comeback at home against the Ohio State Buckeyes. The Buckeyes dominated the game for 45 minutes, had opportunity after opportunity to put the Longhorns away, and missed all of them.

COLLEGE FOOTBALL’S CHAOS ERA IS HERE: TEXAS RALLIES, OREGON FALLS AND LANE KIFFIN EYES RETURN TO OLE MISS

Even Texas Tech, which seemed set up to run through an easy schedule, struggled on the road against Oregon State before pulling away late in the fourth quarter.

Mostly, the week served as a reminder of what makes college football great: big-name teams playing other big-name teams in incredible environments at historic stadiums. The inherently lesser talent at the collegiate level making come-from-behind wins more possible. And stakes, with wins and losses that matter.

It was also a reminder that in the era of the expanded College Football Playoff, these games are becoming less and less common. Because of misplaced incentives, the rise of superconferences, and a selection committee whose criteria for picking teams are nebulous and ever-shifting at best, and bewildering and incomprehensible at worst.

Legendary head coach Nick Saban, speaking on ESPN's "College GameDay" on Saturday, had some suggestions on how to improve the playoff process and encourage more of these matchups: strength of schedule.

"Players love to play in big games," Saban said. "That’s what great competitors love to do. Fans love to see big games."

"I think what we’ve created now is a system of how many games you win helps you get into playoffs, and the playoffs become the barometer for the success of your program," he continued. "We need a better metric to actually evaluate quality wins and quality losses. Some losses are better than some wins."

That's become a familiar suggestion, particularly from SEC supporters as it moves to nine conference games, guaranteeing an additional eight losses per season spread around the conference. It also makes some obvious sense. Of course, Ohio State shouldn't be punished much for losing to Texas, and that result should carry more weight than a win over Youngstown State.

But this mentality is an accidental argument for the type of evaluation that was used in the BCS era, which fans and many coaches eventually hated. Humans have subjective biases or preferences, and they incorporate those biases and preferences into their rankings. Efficiency-driven rankings do have subjective opinions baked into their underlying model assumptions, but that's less subject to on-field, "eye test" bias than poll rankings.

Still, a blend of success rate and efficiency-based computer-driven rankings and strength-of-resume results might create exactly the system Saban wants. Though it might not create the results he expects.

The 2025 Alabama season is an ideal example. They weren't punished for a blowout loss to the Georgia Bulldogs in the SEC Championship Game. Though they should have been. Not just because of the outcome, but because of how it happened, particularly considering their full season resume.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

After their blowout playoff loss, the Crimson Tide ranked 20th in SP+, an efficiency ranking that doesn't care if you win or lose, it cares how you play, adjusted for the competition you're playing against. Their strength of resume was 19th. They weren't a playoff team, considering their performance against their schedule. Would Saban still be happy with the rankings if it hurts his former team?

The result of this year's Texas-Ohio State game is another fantastic example. By postgame win expectancy, the game was effectively a draw. Texas had a 50.2% win expectancy, with an adjusted scoring margin of 0.0. The teams were nearly identical. In SP+, Ohio State ranks second; Texas ranks sixth, even after the win. Ohio State is still expected to be the better team moving forward, based on how the two have played.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

item.title: Charlie Kirk statue defaced with red paint, Jesus crossed out days after 1-year mark of assassination
item.description: Red paint was smeared across the Charlie Kirk statue at Turning Point USA's Phoenix headquarters, with a Christian tribute defaced days after unveiling.
item.content:encoded:
Vandals smeared bright red paint across a newly unveiled statue of Charlie Kirk and defaced a Christian tribute outside Turning Point USA’s Phoenix headquarters early Sunday, just three days after the memorial was installed.

Images from the headquarters show red paint streaked across the eight-foot statue’s face and neck, with a crude frowning face drawn across its chest.

A sign at the base of the statue bearing Kirk’s image and the words "Jesus defeated death so you can live" was also targeted. The word "Jesus" and an image of a cross appeared to be crossed out, while "Satan" was apparently scrawled across the display.

REMEMBERING CHARLIE KIRK: TURNING POINT USA'S ANDREW KOLVET REFLECTS ON CONSERVATIVE GROUP'S CHALLENGING YEAR

Kirk's widow, Erika, who now serves as Turning Point USA CEO, responded with a defiant vow to rebuild, saying the vandals would not erase her husband’s legacy or silence Christians. 

"Charlie once said we should be building two statues for every statue that they tear down," Erika Kirk wrote, adding that her husband’s instinct was always to create rather than destroy.

She said the bullet that killed her husband only amplified his voice and predicted the spray paint would spread his legacy even further. She also vowed to restore the statue, replace Jesus Christ’s name on the damaged sign and continue the movement her husband built.

"God will not be mocked," Erika Kirk wrote.

Phoenix police confirmed to Fox News Digital that the department began receiving calls around 8:09 a.m. reporting vandalism to a memorial in the area of 4900 East Beverly Road.

"Officers have responded to the location, and the incident is under investigation," police said.

No arrests or suspect descriptions had been announced as of Sunday afternoon.

"This morning we woke up to radical criminals vandalizing our headquarters," Turning Point USA Chief Operating Officer Tyler Bowyer wrote on social media. "Crossing over Charlie’s face, scratching out Jesus and the Cross and spraying red paint on his neck.

"This isn’t the country we want to live in," Bowyer added. "Arizona is not Gotham."

INSIDE CHARLIE KIRK’S EFFORT TO DEVELOP THE NEXT GENERATION OF CONSERVATIVE VOICES

Bowyer, who went to the headquarters as police investigated, said TPUSA was prepared to clean the memorial as soon as authorities released the scene.

"God bless the police as they investigate the violent thugs who did this," Bowyer wrote.

TPUSA also released video showing the damage and encouraged its supporters to vote ahead of the midterm elections.

"Hate cannot win," the organization wrote. "The radical Left is showing up to vote. What are you doing to save the country from this?"

In a follow-up statement, TPUSA said it would restore the statue and replace the damaged signs while reviewing footage of the incident and working with law enforcement to identify those responsible.

"Vandalism like this is not funny, it’s diabolical," the organization wrote. "The incident happened in the middle of the night because evil never sleeps."

TPUSA said the vandals went beyond spraying Kirk’s face and neck with red paint, accusing them of making an "intentional decision" to cross out Jesus’ name on the nearby sign.

The organization ended its response by quoting John 15:18: "If the world hates you, keep in mind that it hated me first."

The vandalism struck only days after TPUSA unveiled the bronze statue Thursday to mark one year since Kirk was assassinated while speaking at Utah Valley University on Sept. 10, 2025.

CHARLIE KIRK STATUE BOUND FOR NY'S TIMES SQUARE AS SCULPTOR DEFIES THREATS AHEAD OF UNVEILING

The statue depicts Kirk wearing his signature "Freedom" T-shirt and cross necklace. Those who knew him said the sculpture captured details down to his wedding ring, according to FOX 10 Phoenix.

Turning Point USA commissioned Utah artist Quintin McCann to create the memorial after he began working on a portrait of Kirk the evening the conservative activist was killed, according to the outlet.

ITALIAN ARTIST UNVEILS CHARLIE KIRK MEMORIAL STATUE HE PLANS TO FEATURE AT TIMES SQUARE

"Someone’s death, who I’ve never met, has never impacted me so much," McCann told FOX 10. "And I’m sure many people can agree. And I just stayed at work that evening and just started sculpting his portrait."

The statue was initially placed outside TPUSA’s headquarters near 48th Street and Beverly Road but was expected to be moved indoors for security reasons by the end of the week, the outlet reported.

REPUBLICAN CONVENTION ATTENDEES SHARE HEARTFELT TRIBUTES TO LATE CHARLIE KIRK ON ASSASSINATION ANNIVERSARY

Conservative voices erupted over the attack, condemning the vandalism as another assault on Kirk’s family, friends and legacy.

"Truly abhorrent," Rep. Abe Hamadeh, R-Ariz., wrote on X. "The Charlie Kirk statue that was just unveiled at Turning Point’s HQ was vandalized overnight with red paint.

"The young people who work at Turning Point don’t deserve this, Charlie’s family doesn’t deserve this, his friends don’t deserve this," Hamadeh added. "The left is intolerant and militant. Evil exists and must be confronted continuously."

Rep. Andy Biggs, R-Ariz., was equally blunt.

"This is absolute evil," Biggs wrote.

Conservative commentator Benny Johnson accused the vandals of trying to intimidate Kirk’s supporters.

"These people are incapable of building anything, all they know is destruction," Johnson wrote. "Keep these demons out of power."

TPUSA contributor Alex Clark said seeing the damage brought her to tears before issuing a dire warning to conservative voters.

"The left wants to tap dance in your blood and throw confetti at your gravestone," Clark wrote. "Vote red in midterms like your life depends on it because it actually does as a conservative."

Turning Point USA Chief of Staff Mikey McCoy urged conservatives to answer the vandalism with faith, invoking Kirk’s willingness to return to hostile campuses and the biblical examples of Stephen and Christ praying for those who persecuted them.

"Then I can surrender all the anger, and pure disgust that I feel at seeing this to a just and holy God," McCoy wrote, saying he would pray instead for the repentance and salvation of those responsible.

"Lord, help our Country," he added. "Open their eyes. Break their hearts. Save them."

Bowyer also blasted Democratic Arizona Gov. Katie Hobbs, accusing her of failing to pursue bipartisanship after Kirk’s killing and pointing to her veto of legislation that would have named Loop 202 in Kirk’s honor.

Hobbs said in her March veto letter that she condemned political violence but argued highway-naming decisions should remain nonpartisan and be handled by the state board responsible for such designations.

Kirk was 31 when he was shot and killed during a TPUSA event at Utah Valley University. 

Tyler Robinson, 23, has pleaded not guilty to aggravated murder and other charges in Kirk’s death. Prosecutors are seeking the death penalty.

Erika Kirk took over as CEO of Turning Point USA after her husband’s assassination. The conservative organization he co-founded in 2012 has continued expanding its network of high school and college chapters since his death.

Anyone with information about the vandalism is asked to contact Phoenix police or Silent Witness at 480-WITNESS.

Fox News Digital has reached out to Turning Point USA and Hobbs’ office for additional information and comment.

item.title: Saints defense has touchdown taken away against Lions after Jared Goff fumble is stunningly overturned

The New Orleans Saints scored a routine defensive touchdown against the Detroit Lions on Sunday afternoon. Or so they thought, or so everyone thought.

With the Lions on top 7-0 early in the second quarter, New Orleans defensive end Chase Young beat his man on the edge and forced what looked to be a routine fumble out of Detroit quarterback Jared Goff. It appeared to be a straightforward fumble given that the ball traveled backward, and Goff's arm did not look to be moving forward.

Saints safety Jonas Sanker ultimately picked up the football and carried it into the end zone untouched to get New Orleans on the scoreboard, but only for a brief moment.

ZAC TAYLOR ADMITS BREAKING NFL CHALLENGE FLAG RULE FOR 8 YEARS AS LEAGUE MAKES CHANGE

The football didn't actually travel forward, but Goff's intention overrules the fact that the ball traveled backward, apparently.

"He had started his throwing motion," Mike Pereira, NFL rules analyst for Fox Sports, explained on the broadcast. "Now, throwing motion is bringing the ball up; forget about the hand at this point going forward. item.description: Over 5,400 legitimate websites now serve fake CAPTCHA scams that trick users into pasting malware commands into Windows Run via ClickFix attacks.
item.content:encoded:
You land on the real website of a local business and a CAPTCHA appears. It looks routine until the page tells you to open Windows Run and paste a command. That should stop you cold.

Security researchers say thousands of legitimate small-business websites have been compromised to spread this malware trap. Here's what to know before a familiar website catches you off guard.
